summary: Klamath National Forest lookout planned on Cottonwood Peak west of Henley in 1912; no other source found, and nothing on the site today.

events.note: Forest Supervisor and ranger looked over the ground for a lookout station and a telephone connection; a plan, not a record of building

evidence.supports: Aug 1912 newspaper: Rider and Gott looking over ground for a lookout station on Cottonwood Peak, west of Henley, linked to telephone line
evidence.quote: looking over the ground with a view to erecting a lookout station on the top of Cottonwood Peak, west of Henley, and connecting it to the telephone line.

evidence.supports: Newspaper: forest supervisor and ranger named
evidence.quote: Forest Supervisor W.B. Rider was here recently with Ranger W. Gott

notes_for_editor: Only one source found: a 1912 newspaper item (Ashland Tidings) reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page. Two web searches found nothing else. firelookout.org's California list and the FFLA data have no Cottonwood Peak entry (Cottonwood Pass in Kings County is a different lookout). The story is about 90 words, under the 120-word guide floor, because nothing else is documented; the story says nothing about construction, staffing or fate. The record coordinates (41.88708, -122.64646) and the status 'unknown' were not checked. Recommend a Klamath National Forest records check before publishing.
